To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GWHI in India decreased from 1992–1993 to 2005–2006, and that the GWHIs in all regions decreased in absolute terms except for the North-Eastern region, but as a percentage of the total inequality in the immunisation status of children, the GWHI increased in the North-Western, North-Eastern and Southern regions.
gender based within household inequality in childhood immunization in India is substantial and it increased in the last decade in some regions.
gender based inequality in the immunisation status of Indian children has declined over time, but still persists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a very neglected issue of gender-based discrimination in immunization in India.
the gender based within household inequality in immunization of Indian children, and the changes over time and across regions.
the following question: Does a girl child receive less immunization than a boy child within the same household in India?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the overall inequality declined in all the Indian regions except in the Southern region and the GWHI increased in three out of six regions.
the GWHI is a significant contributor to overall inequality in immunizations and the contribution of GWHI to overall inequality is increasing over time in some of the regions.
the gender based within household inequality in immunization is an important contributor to the overall inequality and that it has not declined over time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while the overall inequality in the status of immunization declined in all regions of the country, the contribution of gender discrimination to overall inequality increased in some regions.
gender based inequality in immunization is a major problem in India, which is getting worse in some regions.
gender based within-households inequality in immunization of Indian children is a serious issue that needs immediate policy attention and action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of gender based within households inequality, the total inequality in immunization in India would be much less than what it is currently.
, in the absence of a comprehensive national strategy, gender based within-households inequality in immunization is likely to persist and may even increase in some regions in the future.
, in order to improve the immunization status of all Indian children, the focus should be on reducing the gender based discrimination within households.
